chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim ibn Mihzam, from Talha ibn Zayd, from the one who raised it, said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'When one of you is brought basil, let him smell it and place it upon his eyes, for it is from Paradise, and when one of you is brought it, let him not reject it.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended etiquette for receiving and using basil according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the Prophet’s (peace be upon him and his family) emphasis on appreciating the sensory blessings of creation, specifically identifying basil as a fragrant plant originating from Paradise. It underscores the Shia tradition of finding spiritual and physical comfort in natural gifts, encouraging believers to accept them with gratitude rather than rejecting them out of modesty or habit.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, and Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Khalid, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Ibrahim Bin Mihzam, from Talha Bin Zayd, from the one who raised it, said,

‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘Whenever one of you is brought the basil, so let him smell it and place it upon his eyes, for it is from the Paradise, and whenever one of you is brought it, so let him not reject it’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid all from ibn Mahbub from Ibrahim ibn Mehzam from Talhah ibn Zayd from the one who has narrated it in a marfu ‘ manner has said the following: “The Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘
If one brings you sweet basil you must smell it and place it on your eyes because it is from the garden (paradises); and if it is brought for you do not reject it.’”
